profile.summary: yiminghe is a mid-level JavaScript developer with deep expertise in jQuery’s DOM and CSS manipulation internals. Their contributions focus on fixing cross-browser inconsistencies in CSS properties (e.g., `opacity`, `left`, `top`) and ensuring consistent behavior across legacy browsers like IE8-10. The developer demonstrates strong skills in CSS value normalization, interactive debugging using JSFiddle, and iterative refinement of jQuery’s core functionality. Their work is narrowly specialized in maintaining jQuery’s reliability in legacy environments, with no evidence of modern JavaScript frameworks or backend systems.
skill_evidence: PR 1: Fixes inconsistent `opacity` behavior across IE < 9 and modern browsers, referencing specific IE quirks in the description
PR 2-4: Repeated attempts to address the same `left`/`top` CSS value inconsistency, showing iterative debugging and refinement
PR 5: Includes a JSFiddle link (`jsfiddle.net/yiminghe/nBRgE/`) to demonstrate the `left`/`top` CSS retrieval bug and verify the fix
PR 5 description: 'since jQuery handles % specially, then it should handle auto too', showing deep understanding of CSS value normalization rules
PR 6: Adds test case (`jsfiddle.net/yiminghe/Yu9sP/5/`) for `auto` value handling in `left`/`top`, emphasizing reproducible debugging
PR 3 mentions 'Adjust code style', indicating attention to jQuery’s coding conventions and iterative maintenance
All PRs involve zero additions/deletions but internal logic changes, suggesting focused fixes to jQuery’s CSS handling internals
PRs reference multiple browsers (IE9, IE10, Chrome, Firefox) in descriptions, proving expertise in cross-browser compatibility
